  "tokenized_directions": [
    {
      "step": 1,
      "text": "The Apician dish is made thus: Take {{ing_01|small pieces of cooked sow’s belly [with the paps on it]}} {{ing_02|pieces of fish}}, {{ing_03|pieces of chicken}}, {{ing_04|the breasts of figpeckers or of thrushes [slightly] cooked}}, [and] whichever is best. Mince all this very carefully, particularly the {{ing_04|figpeckers}} [the meat of which is very tender]. Dissolve in {{ing_05|oil}} {{ing_06|strictly fresh eggs}}; crush {{ing_07|pepper}} and {{ing_08|lovage}}, pour over some {{ing_09|broth}} and {{ing_10|raisin wine}}, put it in a saucepan to heat and bind with {{ing_11|roux}}. After you have cut all in regular pieces, let it come to the boiling point. When done, retire [from the fire] with its juice of which you put some in another deep pan with {{ing_13|whole pepper}} and {{ing_14|pignolia nuts}}. Spread [the ragout] out in single layers with {{ing_12|thin pancakes}} in between; put in as many {{ing_12|pancakes}} and layers of meat as is required to fill the dish; put a final cover of {{ing_12|pancake}} on top and sprinkle with {{ing_07|pepper}} after those {{ing_15|eggs}} have been added [which serve] to tie the dish. Now put this [mould or dish] in a boiler [steamer, hot water bath, allow to congeal] and dish it out [by unmoulding it]. An expensive silver platter would enhance the appearance of this dish materially."
    }
